newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ATD, NTUC Income in S$50 mln venture.
newsitem.headline: ATD, NTUC Income in S$50 mln venture.

text.p: Alliance Technology and Development Ltd (ATD) and NTUC Income Insurance Cooperative Ltd (Income) said on Friday they would invest Singapore $50 million in joint venture leisure resort developments.
"We have got about S$50 million for the first phase of our developments," said Lim Chee Yong, chief executive of ATD.
"The first four resorts will be rolled out over the next two years," he told reporters at a signing ceremony for the joint venture deal.
The new company, Nuansa Leisure Pte Ltd, will be a unit of ATD operating under the name of Club Nuansa.
Income will hold a 40 percent stake in the S$10 million capitalised firm and supply 40 percent of the investment capital required to develop the first phase resorts.

Its first four resorts are a S$22 million site on the Singapore island of Pulau Ubin, an Australian $10.9 million site on the Gold Coast and a A$6.8 million site near Cairns in Australia, and 29 suites of the Crown Prince Hotel in Penang, Malaysia.
Further resorts in Australian wine region Hunter Valley, Bali and Lombok in Indonesia and Phuket in Thailand could follow within five years if the initial response was good, Lim said.
Club Nuansa plans to attract 2,000 members in the first two years with between 500 and 1,000 joining through a special incentive scheme offered to Income policyholders.
Membership charges would probably be about S$20,000 giving membership for 30 years and returning the capital to members after this period, Income chief executive Tan Kin Lian said.
Membership levels are planned to rise to about 12,000 over five years by which time Club Nuansa would need 20 to 30 resort locations to cater for members' needs, Tan said.
"By this time I expect the business to be a $500 million firm," said Lim, whose ATD has several leisure projects under management, including Singapore's Fort Canning Country Club.
"If the membership drive is successful, which we expect it to be, then we expect it (Club Nuansa) to be a substantial contributor to earnings," Lim said.
